scores.notes: Jesus stands in the stern with an arm out over the water while the disciples look up at him and the sea settles under a clearing sky; full-bleed paint, no marks or extra people.
Saul kneels shielding his eyes under a wash of light with companions recoiling and Damascus behind, but the roadside milestone at right carries capital letters reading roughly 'RONAN MILETE'.
Jesus cries out and points at the rock tomb before a startled crowd while the wrapped Lazarus steps from the doorway (face uncovered, one verse early); no lettering, frame or anatomy problems.
Light rays break through dark cloud over a formless sea with no figure of any kind; small ragged slivers of bare paper show on the left and right edges, which this item accepts.

Holmes holds the blue stone to the window light with Watson by the fire, but the open strong box on the desk already holds several more blue stones, the desk and shelf papers carry rows of unreadable pseudo-script, and Holmes is styled as the modern television Sherlock (tousled dark curls, long dark greatcoat with turned-up collar and scarf). Flagged on costume and styling; I do not name an actor from the face.
Samuel pours oil from a horn onto the kneeling young David with Jesse and the brothers standing round and a soft radiance from the sky; nothing written, no frame, hands and feet sound.

Hezekiah stands in the temple court as workers carry sacks and jars into the storerooms beside the bronze basin on oxen; pale areas at top left are painted cloud, and the door carvings are ornament, not writing.
Peter leaps from the boat clutching his coat while a disciple points to the small figure of Jesus by a fire on shore and the others haul the full net; pale top is painted sky, no marks.
The Israelites walk the dry seabed between two towering walls of water with Moses and his staff at the front; bare white paper shows at the bottom corners and side edges, accepted for this item.
Job sits on the ash heap among potsherds looking up at a huge whirlwind with his friends cowering beside him; the whirlwind holds no face or body, and nothing is written.
The man kneels with a knife over the dead woman laid on a mat inside his house, donkey and bundle at the open door; restrained with no blood or cutting shown, full-bleed, no marks.
A disciple shakes Jesus awake on the cushion in the stern while others bail and fight the sail in the storm; a strip of bare cream paper runs down the left edge, accepted here.

Four soldiers cast lots on a flat stone beside his folded garments with the crucified Jesus behind, shown without gore; the nine small round lot tokens each carry a tiny glyph-like mark (unreadable, pip-like), and the bottom corners fade to bare paper (accepted).

March Hare and Hatter lean over the sleeping Dormouse at one corner of the long tea table while a scowling Alice sits in the big armchair at the end, tree and house behind; left and right edges and corners are bare white paper (accepted), nothing written.
Saul staggers under a shaft of light from the clouds, bag and staff dropped, with companions on both sides shielding their eyes and Damascus on the road ahead; full-bleed, no lettering.

Daniel watches rows of empty flaming thrones and burning wheels around a blaze of white light above ranked multitudes; the Ancient of Days is light only, with no face, body or robe, and nothing is written.

Holmes tosses the great ball of papers up toward the rack with Watson opposite in the empty carriage, matching the text; the scattered newspapers show columns of print-like marks and the two brass wall plaques show blurred text lines, all unreadable. No likeness call made from the face.

The King peers from behind Alice at the floating Cheshire Cat head while the Queen sweeps past without looking round, flamingo and hedgehogs on the lawn; the only marks are heart pips on the King's playing-card back and tunic (card pips, unreadable), no words or numerals.

The man kneels with a knife beside the shrouded body of the woman on straw inside the stone house; sombre and bloodless, with ragged bare paper at the corners and side edges (accepted) and nothing written.

Alice, the sleepy Dormouse, March Hare and Hatter sit at the tea table as in the text, but the Hatter's large pocket watch at right shows legible dial numerals (12, 1, 3, 4, 9, 10); pale top right is painted sky, not bare paper.
Daniel raises a refusing hand and points to the blank plaster wall before the enthroned king amid banquet tables and courtiers; the wall bears no writing and there are no other marks.

Moses stands on a rock with his hand stretched over the sea as a gale bends the palms and drives the water back, the people and animals waiting behind; no divine figure, painted to every edge, no lettering.

The huge masked visitor in blue cloak with flame lining, astrakhan bands, brooch and fur-topped boots enters as Holmes stands by the window and Watson sits in the armchair; a sheet pinned to the bookcase and loose papers carry faint lines of unreadable pseudo-script (he also holds a bag rather than his hat, and a modern-looking wall switch is at right). No likeness call made from the face.

An empty radiant throne stands over a glassy floor with the four winged, eye-covered creatures (lion, calf, man-faced, eagle) and crowned elders, with no figure of God; but a robed man with a staff stands prominently in the right foreground as the seer, whom this verse does not call for.

Bradstreet leans from the carriage to question the station-master while a great column of smoke rises behind the trees, as described; the sheet in the station-master's hand has a bold header of garbled pseudo-letters over a ruled table of squiggles (unreadable), and the right side and corners fade to bare white paper (accepted).
Moses strikes the rock with his rod and water pours out as Aaron watches and the people, camels, sheep and goats drink; the corners and edges are bare white paper (accepted) and nothing is written.

Holmes sits alone by the fire with steepled fingers, a fair reading of the reflective opening with no Irene Adler drawn; the papers beside him carry lines of pseudo-script and the mantel clock face has dial marks, all unreadable. No likeness call made from the face.

A wheeled throne burns in a column of white light and smoke with no figure on it, other thrones occupied by seated men, a vast multitude standing, and Daniel watching at right; no human form for the Ancient of Days and nothing written.
Alice wags a reproving finger at the wide-eyed Hatter holding cup and bread while the March Hare pours tea at the long laid table under the tree; no lettering on hat or crockery, hands sound.
Job sits on the ash heap with potsherds and staff, gazing up at a towering whirlwind over the plain with city walls beyond; the whirlwind is only cloud and dust, no figure, no writing.

Four soldiers crouch casting small dice-like lots over the garments with three crosses behind, shown without blood; the board above the central cross is blank, the dice show no distinct marks and the pale left side is painted sky.

Four soldiers kneel dividing cloths and dropping lots, but the crucified man directly above them still wears his full tunic and blue mantle, contradicting the garments being shared out below; no lettering, and the pale top left is painted cloud.
Egyptian chariots and horsemen charge down the seabed between two walls of water, a long column behind them; no divine figure, no writing, horses and drivers read correctly.

The father gestures to his servants as they bring the robe, a ring on a dish and sandals to the ragged son in the courtyard; the top-left corner and upper edge fade to bare paper (accepted), nothing written.

The King stands by Alice, who holds her flamingo, gesturing warily at the floating Cat head while the Queen points away and a hedgehog trots past; a background card soldier is a five of hearts with pips and a tiny corner index squiggle and others wear club pips (card pips, unreadable). Two small background attendants read as people in pip tunics rather than flat cards, too minor to call a rule break; top right is bare paper (accepted).

Hatherley, hands bandaged, points excitedly at the burning house across the gravel drive and rose bushes with the crowd and fire engines, Holmes and Watson beside him; painted to the edges with no lettering. No likeness call made from the face.

In the vaulted cellar Holmes holds the lantern among the crates with two men behind him while Watson crouches behind a crate with his revolver laid on top; the crates are unmarked and nothing is written (a faint face-like smudge in the ceiling shadow is not prominent).

A bearded teacher with blank scrolls addresses a seated group in a Greek city: the letter's author drawn speaking his own words, with no mirror, dim reflection or face-to-face meeting anywhere in the picture; scrolls carry no marks.

Daniel lifts a hand in refusal and points toward the wall before the enthroned king and his courtiers; the wall panel is left blank white with no writing, the tapestry and lion friezes are ornament, and the outer edges are painted.
Peter steps from the bow onto the waves toward Jesus, who stands on the water with an open hand, the others watching from the boat under a storm sky; no lettering, limbs sound.

Alice studies the little bottle beside the glass table with its gold key, the curtained small door and the lamp-lit hall of doors, as described; the bottle's paper label carries rows of tiny squiggles standing in for writing (unreadable). Painted to the edges.
